newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Rebels get Guatemala's first post-war amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Rebels get Guatemala's first post-war amnesty.

text.p: Two Guatemalan guerrillas became the first rebels to benefit from an amnesty included in peace accords which ended a 36-year war, lawyers said on Tuesday.
The Guatemalan Lawyers Association, which made the succesful amnesty appeals for the two men, said they were absolved of illegal arms possession and treason charges.
February Timoteo Navarijo, serving a prison sentence for treason, was released recently in the first application, Lesbia Tevalan Castellanos, president of the lawyers' association, told Reuters.
An appeals court judge on Monday also let off Hugo Lemus, who was on probation for illegal arms possession.

Both men were members of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG), the rebel group that on Dec. 29 signed an historic peace treaty with the government, ending Central America's last and longest civil conflict.
The peace accords included a limited amnesty for guerrilla fighters and military personnel who committed political crimes, such as rebellion and sedition.
